Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

after preposition

a time or an event

also after dinner, after lunch, after two days, a few days later, afterwards

classical

Plin. Ep. 9.36.4: post cēnam cōmoedia aut lyristēs
Quint. 11.2.17: post tempus reversī

post + acc.

preposition with the accusative

With a time or an event: post cēnam, post merīdiem, post diēs decem. A thing is not a point in time: for “after the film” or “after the train” Latin says what happened, with a clause (postquam) or a participle (quō factō, when that was done).

Other words

  • paucīs post diēbus — a few days later, a few days after

    phrase: post as an adverb, with the measure of time in the ablative · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 5.20.3: interiit paucīs post diēbus; Cic. Sen. 19: novem annīs post meum cōnsulātum

    So paulō post, a little later; multīs post annīs, many years later.

Examples

  • cēnantī mihi, sī cum uxōre vel paucīs, liber legitur; post cēnam cōmoedia aut lyristēs; mox cum meīs ambulō

    at dinner, if I am with my wife or a few friends, a book is read aloud; after dinner, a comedy or a lyre-player; then I take a walk with my householdPlin. Ep. 9.36.4

  • post sōlis ortum fulgidī sērum est cubīle spernere

    once the bright sun is up, it is late to be leaving one’s bedPrud. Cath. 1.9–10

  • Post diēs autem decem, appāruērunt vultūs eōrum meliōrēs, et corpulentiōrēs

    after ten days their faces looked better and plumperDan. 1.15

  • nam cum in loca aliqua post tempus reversī sumus, nōn ipsa agnōscimus tantum, sed etiam, quae in hīs fēcerīmus, reminīscimur

    when we go back to a place after some time, we not only recognise it, but remember what we did thereQuint. 11.2.17

  • commodum discesserās heri cum Trebātius vēnit, paulō post Curtius

    you had only just left yesterday when Trebatius came, and a little later CurtiusCic. Att. 13.9.1

  • quae crēbrius inter sē pugnābunt, aspargī eās oportet aquā mulsā. quō factō nōn modo dēsistunt pugnā, sed etiam conferciunt sē lingentēs

    bees that keep fighting should be sprinkled with honey-water; after that they not only stop fighting but huddle together, licking each otherVarr. RR 3.16.35

See also before, later, since.
